summary: Khenpo Konchog Gyaltsen Rinpoche is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied under traditional teachers Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen, Khyunga Rinpoche, and Pachung Rinpoche.
Khenpo Lodrö Dönyö works in the fields of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Kalu Rinpoche and Bokar Rinpoche, and also taught Kalu Rinpoche.

Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang (1879–1941) was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied under numerous teachers, including Nyo Shul Lungtok Tenpé Gyaltsen from circa 1894 to 1901, and taught figures such as Chatral Sangye Dorje and Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen.
Khenpo Nüden studied under Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang and Shechen Gyaltsab, and taught Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen.
Khenpo Sherab Püntsok studied under Ogyen Trinley Dorje and Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche.

Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche (1934–2024) worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied under Lama Zopa Tarchin, Lama Zolpa Trinlé, and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje (~1960–1981), later serving as principal teacher at Rumtek Monastery (~1977) and spiritual advisor at Pullahari Monastery (1992).

Khetsun Sangpo Rinpoche (1920–2009) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under teachers including Jetsun Lochen Rinpoche, Dudjom Rinpoche, and Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, taught at the University of Tokyo and Kyoto University (1960–1970), and founded Nyingmapa Wishfulfilling Center in 1971.

Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen (1895–1977) worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology, studying at Rumtek Monastery and under numerous teachers. He held teaching posts at Men-Tsee-Khang in Lhasa and at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University circa 1957, and taught the 14th Dalai Lama.
Khyenrab Norbu (1882–1962) was a Tibetology scholar. He studied under Tré Khang Jampa Tubwang, Tsipa Ngawo Ché, Drung Yik Rabten, and Tso Jé Dorjé Gyaltsen, and taught Yeshi Donden among others.

id: P:Khyungpo Gyal Tön Rinpoche Karma Orgyen Jikme Chökyi Sengé
summary: Khyungpo Gyal Tön Rinpoche Karma Orgyen Jikme Chökyi Sengé studied under Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang and Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö.
Ki-yong Rhi (1922–1996) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who held positions at Dongguk University, where he was attested in 1983 and as professor emeritus in 2007.

Kiattisak Ponampon works in Buddhist studies. He completed an MA at the University of Otago attested in 2015 under supervisors Xiaohuan Zhao, Will Sweetman, and Elizabeth Guthrie, and studied under Jinhua Chen, Stephen R. Bokenkamp, and others in 2013.

Kichinosuke Ito (1885–1961) was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo and University of Freiburg. He taught at the University of Tokyo (1911–1918; professor 1923–1945), Hokkaido University (1947, 1950–1951), and Chuo University (1951–1958).
Kien T. Le specializes in Buddhist studies. Le studied for an MDiv at Harvard University (2023–2026) and became a PhD student at Indiana University Bloomington in 2026.
Kim Gutschow specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned a PhD at Harvard University and held a teaching post at Wesleyan University.
Kim Knott is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. She held posts at the University of Leeds (circa 1984–2012) and Lancaster University (circa 2012).
Kim Lam specializes in Buddhist studies and religious studies. Lam has held positions at Deakin University's Melbourne Burwood Campus and as a Research Officer at Western Sydney University.

Kim Plofker is an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who completed a PhD at Brown University under David Pingree in 1995. She held appointments at Brown, MIT, Utrecht University, and Union College, where she became associate professor in 2019.

Kimberley C. Patton is a religious studies scholar who completed her dissertation at Harvard University (circa 1984–1992). She taught at Harvard as assistant professor (circa 1991–1999) and professor (from circa 1999), and was an associate at ASCSA in 1991.

Kimiaki Tanaka is an Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and Oxford. He served as research assistant at the University of Tokyo (circa 1984–1988) and held appointments at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.
